newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad sees rate rise for year end.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad sees rate rise for year end.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan electricity company Electricidad de Caracas sees the possibility of a tariff rise towards the end of the year, company sources said.

"The government hasn't promised anything," said a high placed source who asked not to be named. "But signs look good for them to make a decision around the end of October on a rise that could be made effective early next year."
Rumors of a possible rate rise have sent the Caracas bolsa's bellwether stock soaring in recent days, with foreign buyers pushing it ahead 9.05 bolivars to close at 429.00 on Tuesday.

Electricidad received rate increases in August and May this year of 9.65 and 28 percent. When company executives complained the hikes fell well behind cost increases, Energy and Mines minister Erwin Arrieta said further rate adjustments might come, depending on the outcome of audits of company accounts.
"I think the minister has recently come to understand things that he didn't before," said the source.
